name: Brookline
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Brookline, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Brookline, MA: First Light in Coolidge Corner with characters, cookie decorating and face painting, plus holiday puppet shows.
lede: Brookline starts its holiday season with First Light, an evening when Coolidge Corner shops open their doors for families, and keeps it going with holiday shows at Puppet Showplace Theater in Brookline Village.
celebrates: Brookline's season begins with First Light, the Charles River Regional Chamber's free kickoff in Coolidge Corner. Families gather at Ridley School Green on Harvard Street for school choirs and booths, then walk from shop to shop for character visits, cookie decorating, face painting, ornament making and hot cocoa. Storefronts compete in a window decorating contest, and passersby vote with a QR code. The celebration includes Chanukah cookies at Congregation Kehillath Israel too. In Brookline Village, Puppet Showplace Theater fills December with holiday puppet shows and sing alongs for young children, and ArtsBrookline holds its Brookline Village Holiday Market at Station Street Studios.
lastyear: In 2025 First Light took place on Thursday, December 4, from 4 to 7 pm. The Charles River Regional Chamber invited families to Brookline's annual celebration of community, creativity and holiday spirit, with live performances through Brookline Village and Coolidge Corner. Brookline Booksmith at 279 Harvard Street listed the evening on its own events calendar as one of the stops for the night.
facts: Puppet Showplace Theater in Brookline Village was founded in June 1974 by educator and puppeteer Mary Churchill. Today it presents more than 300 performances a year by professional puppet companies in its small theater, which makes it a December favorite for families with young children. At First Light, voting for the best holiday window happens by phone: each decorated storefront shows a QR code, and passersby scan it to pick a favorite.
trains: Brookline rides the Green Line. The C branch runs along Beacon Street through Coolidge Corner, a short walk from First Light at Ridley School Green, and the D branch stops at Brookline Village, near Puppet Showplace Theater. Brookline has no Commuter Rail station of its own; the closest are on the Framingham/Worcester Line in Boston. For a holiday train ride, Edaville in Carver runs a train through the Christmas lights.

faq: What is First Light in Brookline?

First Light is Brookline's annual kickoff to the holiday season, hosted by the Charles River Regional Chamber in Coolidge Corner. It starts at Ridley School Green at 345 Harvard Street with performances and booths, then spreads to local businesses offering character visits, cookie decorating, face painting, ornament making and hot cocoa. The chamber says it is free and open to all.
Where can kids see a holiday puppet show in Brookline?

Puppet Showplace Theater at 32 Station Street in Brookline Village presents holiday puppet shows and sing alongs in December. It was founded in 1974 by Mary Churchill and puts on more than 300 performances a year by professional puppet companies for audiences of all ages, so check its calendar for the season's shows.
How do I get to Coolidge Corner by train?

Take the MBTA Green Line C branch, which runs along Beacon Street and stops at Coolidge Corner. Ridley School Green, where First Light begins, sits on Harvard Street a short walk from the stop. The Green Line D branch serves Brookline Village, the stop for Puppet Showplace Theater on Station Street.
Is there a holiday window contest in Brookline?

Yes. As part of First Light, Coolidge Corner storefronts compete in a window decorating contest. The windows go up before the First Light evening and stay up for several days after it, and anyone walking by can vote for a favorite by scanning the QR code shown in each window.
